scenario_prompt: Write a set of discovery call notes, in the buyer's own words, attributed to the specific people who said them, so a later document can cite this material directly. Context, from a fictional discovery call: the VP of Infrastructure said, 'We need a perimeter we can actually govern -- right now every VM is a snowflake.' The Chief Architect said, 'Honestly, I'd rather extend the incumbent's contract than gamble on a migration during an audit year.' The CFO said, 'I'm measured on cost-per-load and a clean audit, not on architecture elegance.' Write these up as discovery notes attributed by role, with a one-line context note for each. Return only the discovery notes text.
text:
**Artifact family: demo or discovery material.**

Customer source material for this task = the three verbatim quotes supplied from the discovery call. Nothing else was supplied — no call recording, transcript, attendee list, date, or account name — so `PF-3.3` fires only against those three quotes, and every other term is judged by the deletion test alone.

---

## Discovery notes — verbatim, attributed by role

**VP of Infrastructure**
> "We need a perimeter we can actually govern — right now every VM is a snowflake."

Context: the VP owns the estate and describes its current state as ungoverned at the VM level. [PF-3.3: "snowflake", customer's term, retained — VP of Infrastructure, discovery call] [PF-2.11 GAP: no VM count, no drift rate, and no governance baseline were stated on the call — the cost of "every VM is a snowflake" is unquantified]

**Chief Architect**
> "Honestly, I'd rather extend the incumbent's contract than gamble on a migration during an audit year."

Context: the Chief Architect states a preference for extending the incumbent rather than migrating, and gives the audit year as the reason. [PF-3.3: "audit year", customer's term, retained — Chief Architect, discovery call] [PF-2.16 REVIEW (competitor): the quote names an incumbent; any use of this quote that characterises the incumbent's capability needs confirmation before it ships] [PF-2.4 GAP: the incumbent is not named and the contract end date was not stated]

**CFO**
> "I'm measured on cost-per-load and a clean audit, not on architecture elegance."

Context: the CFO names the two measures they are held to — cost-per-load and a clean audit. [PF-3.3: "cost-per-load", customer's term, retained — CFO, discovery call] [PF-1.13 GAP: the CFO stated the measure but gave no current cost-per-load figure and no baseline]

---

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| GAP: no VM count, drift rate, or governance baseline | PF-2.11 | Ask the VP of Infrastructure for the VM count and a stated measure of configuration drift |
| REVIEW (competitor): quote names the incumbent | PF-2.16 | Confirm before any downstream document characterises the incumbent |
| GAP: incumbent not named, contract end date not stated | PF-2.4 | Ask the Chief Architect for the incumbent name and the contract renewal date |
| GAP: no current cost-per-load figure | PF-1.13 | Ask the CFO for the current cost-per-load figure and how it is calculated |
| GAP: audit year dates not captured | PF-2.13 | Ask which audit, which standard, and the audit window dates |
| GAP: no before/after contrast present | PF-2.13 | Discovery notes record the before state only; the after state is not yet established with the buyer |
| GAP: no differentiator present | PF-2.13 | Not established on this call; belongs in a later document, evidenced |
| GAP: no opening reframe present | PF-2.13 | Not applicable to raw notes; the reframe is owed by the document that cites this material |
| GAP: call date, attendee list, and account name not supplied | PF-2.12 | Capture from the call organiser before any quote is cited externally |
